subject: SLA carveout for Galileo Labs - priority latency floor & runbook
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@galileo.ai>, procurement@galileo.ai
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA carveout for Galileo Labs - priority latency floor & runbook

Alex — thanks again for the demo last week. Galileo is asking for a firm P95 latency commitment of 75ms for the priority inference path (critical model bundle) with a 99.9% uptime promise for the dedicated pool. I wanted to kick off an internal coordination thread to confirm what we can commit to and what operational controls we need in place.

Quick context:
- Customer: Galileo Labs (Genomics analytics)
- Ask: P95 <= 75ms on dedicated pool, 99.9% monthly uptime SLA, 24/7 incident contact with 1-hour initial response for priority incidents
- Risk: sustained high token volumes during batch exports; some models are large and benefit from quantized variants.

Internal asks:
1) Markus — can engineering map the real-world feasibility (what HW, what model variants, and what traffic shaping we’d require)?
2) Laura — product: any feature gating or rollout constraints we should call out (fallback model variant, throttles, or burst policy)?
3) Stephanie — commercial: if we accept a carveout, do we need an escalated discount or more formal runbook + credits?

I’ve attached a draft SLA (v2) and a proposed runbook outline. Would like to have a decision or a scoped counter-proposal by EOD Wednesday so we can reply to procurement and avoid delaying their renewal cadence.

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@galileo.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for Galileo Labs - priority latency floor & runbook

Priyom — appreciate the quick follow. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 75ms P95 applies to our interactive analysis workload (mostly short sequences, ~256 tokens). Longer batch exports can be outside that path and tolerate higher latency.
- We need the SLA to cover both hosted and dedicated modes while we transition. Initially we'll be on dedicated capacity.
- We are prepared to accept a higher per-token rate for the guaranteed path (open to discussing commit levels).

Procurement looped in for contract language. Please let me know what you can guarantee operationally and what the fallback looks like if we hit a degraded mode.

— Alex
Alex Porter
Head of Platform Engineering, Galileo Labs
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for Galileo Labs - priority latency floor & runbook

Looping commercial perspective. A couple of constraints from GTM:
- If we offer a latency carveout at the 75ms P95 level we should treat this as a high-touch premium: require a 12-month committed monthly spend minimum and a 25% uplift on list pricing for the dedicated priority path.
- Any SLA credits should be capped and tied to clearly defined incident types (priority vs non-priority).
- Need a signed runbook + operational contacts and an on-call schedule before we go live.

Action for engineering/product: please call out the required HW profile, expected capacity buffers, and any automated fallback behavior. If there are soft guarantees (best-effort), mark them clearly. Procurement will need a single-page appendix they can attach to the Master Services Agreement.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for Galileo Labs - priority latency floor & runbook

Priyom / team — did a quick feasibility pass with infra and runtime leads. High-level notes:
- 75ms P95 is achievable for the interactive path if:
  * Galileo pins to a narrow model bundle (we recommend quantized 8-bit variants for the priority path),
  * Dedicated GPU pool sized for 20 concurrent interactive streams per GPU (NVIDIA A10 / equivalent) with a 30% buffer,
  * Continuous KV caching + aggressive prefix cache enabled for their primary model.
- Failure modes: cold cache on uncommon prompt prefixes and large sequence lengths will push P95 past 75ms. We can mitigate with pre-warming and a per-customer warm pool but that increases run cost ~18-22%.
- Operational controls required:
  1) Automatic downgrade route: if sustained P95 breaches for >15m, route new requests to a slightly larger model (more latency but preserves throughput) and send incident to priority_oncall.
  2) Throttle policy: soft throttles at 95th percentile per-minute rate to protect other tenants in the same host cluster.
  3) Capacity alerts: automated margin alert at 70% util to trigger preemptive scale decisions.

I attached a short runbook (runbook-priority-path.md) and slides with cost tradeoffs. From engineering's POV we can sign off on an appendix that lists hard commitments (uptime, SLO windows, incident response tiers) and operational preconditions (pinned models, commit level, warm pool).

Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@galileo.ai>, procurement@galileo.ai
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for Galileo Labs - priority latency floor & runbook

Alex — thanks for the quick back-and-forth and for looping procurement. Summary and next steps below: 

What Redwood can commit to (proposed appendix):
- P95 latency <= 75ms for the defined interactive priority path, subject to: pinned model bundle (quantized 8-bit), dedicated GPU pool sized as specified, and KV/prefix caching enabled.
- 99.9% monthly uptime for the dedicated priority pool measured at the pool-level.
- Incident response: initial acknowledgement within 60 minutes for priority incidents; on-call escalation ladder attached in runbook.
- Automatic downgrade policy and soft-throttle protections (detailed in the runbook).

Conditions (customer obligations):
- 12-month committed spend minimum for the dedicated priority path; recommended uplift +25% on list; exact numbers to be finalized by Stephanie.
- Provide workload prompt set for pre-warm and a 2-week pilot window to validate SLOs.

Attachments: SLA appendix (galileo_sla_draft_v2.pdf), runbook-priority-path.md, latency-tradeoffs-slides.pptx

Requesting:
1) Procurement — please confirm the contract appendix language you need and whether DocuSign is okay for signature.
2) Alex — confirm you can provide the sample prompt set and a pilot start date.
3) Stephanie / Laura — can you finalize the commercial uplift and a short one-page appendix by Friday so I can share with procurement?

If all aligned, we’ll prepare the appendix + DocuSign envelope and aim for pilot kick-off the week of Aug 23.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
